title: AI Builders Digest
subtitle: Bilingual edition · 双语对照版

intro.text: 今天有两条主线。一条是竞争：OpenAI 宣布终止通过 Cursor 提供模型访问，Replit 和 Anthropic 立刻接盘表态，AI 编程工具的格局正在剧烈重组。另一条是更底层的主题：Eon 两位创始人在播客里说，模型和算力都已接近商品化，数据才是 AI 时代真正的护城河；而多位资深 builder 不约而同地提醒，这个行业的信念半衰期已经短到只有几个月。再加上 Vercel CEO 对 web 两极化的判断，今天的拼图指向同一个方向——工具会换、格局会变，只有数据和快速迭代的能力是确定的。

archive.title: 护城河与半衰期
archive.desc: AI 编程工具格局剧烈重组，而多位 builder 指向同一个结论：数据是真正的护城河，信念的半衰期越来越短。

footerNote: Source: Follow Builders curated daily digest. Rebuilt from the 2026-08-23 source feeds.

sections.title: OpenAI Cuts Ties with Cursor / OpenAI 与 Cursor 分道扬镳
sections.desc: 一条声明引爆了 AI 编程工具圈的站队：OpenAI 宣布终止通过 Cursor 提供模型访问，Replit 与 Anthropic 立刻表态。

rewrite: OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux, who leads Codex and ChatGPT, announced that OpenAI is ending its partnership with Cursor, stopping model access effective November 12. The bluntly stated reason: 'It boils down to trust.'

The announcement, which drew over 5,600 likes, reads like a breakup letter to developers: OpenAI will keep letting people use their own API key in Cursor and via OpenAI's IDE extensions, and it promises to keep working with 'the broadest range of tools and harnesses.'

The subtext is a distribution war: OpenAI is pulling its frontier models out of a rival coding platform to push developers toward its own Codex and ChatGPT surfaces, while claiming to stay tool-agnostic.
original: We unfortunately have decided that we cannot continue providing access to our models through Cursor and are ending our partnership. It boils down to trust and we've asked that this takes effect on November 12 to give you some time to plan.
We will continue to allow using your own OpenAI API key and similarly will continue to provide access through our IDE extensions for Cursor.

rewrite: OpenAI 负责 Codex 和 ChatGPT 的 Thibault Sottiaux 宣布：OpenAI 将终止与 Cursor 的合作，从 11 月 12 日起停止通过 Cursor 提供模型访问。理由直白得近乎冷硬——「说到底就是信任问题」。
这条声明拿了 5600 多个赞，读起来像一封给开发者的分手信：OpenAI 会继续允许你在 Cursor 里用你自己的 API key，也继续通过官方 IDE 插件提供访问，并承诺继续与「最广泛的工具和 harness 阵营」合作。
潜台词是一场分发战争：OpenAI 把旗舰模型从一个竞争性的编程平台上撤走，把开发者推向自家的 Codex 和 ChatGPT 界面，同时嘴上仍说自己「保持工具中立」。
original: 很遗憾我们决定不再通过 Cursor 提供模型访问，并终止合作。说到底就是信任问题，我们要求在 11 月 12 日生效，给你留出规划时间。
我们会继续允许你在 Cursor 里使用你自己的 OpenAI API key，也会继续通过官方 IDE 插件提供访问。

rewrite: Replit CEO Amjad Masad moved fast: within hours he pointed out you can access OpenAI models on Replit for free, and that Replit's router makes high-end models 'incredibly cost-efficient.'
The sharper pitch came next: if you're a business looking for 'an independent, multi-model alternative to Cursor, we'd be happy to fund your transition.'

This is classic platform arbitrage: when a big vendor closes a distribution channel, rivals rush to subsidize the switch. The OpenAI-Cursor split instantly became a customer-acquisition moment for every multi-model coding tool.
original: You can access OpenAI models on Replit for free.
If you're a business looking for an independent, multi-model alternative to Cursor, we'd be happy to fund your transition.

rewrite: Replit CEO Amjad Masad 反应极快：几个小时内就指出，你可以在 Replit 上免费访问 OpenAI 模型，而且 Replit 的路由让高端模型变得「极其划算」。
更狠的招在后面：如果你是一家想找「独立、多模型的 Cursor 替代品」的公司，「我们很乐意资助你的迁移」。
这是典型的平台套利：当大厂关闭一条分发渠道，对手立刻冲上来补贴换平台。OpenAI 与 Cursor 的分手，瞬间变成了所有多模型编程工具的获客时刻。
original: 你可以在 Replit 上免费访问 OpenAI 模型。
如果你是找独立、多模型 Cursor 替代品的公司，我们很乐意资助你的迁移。

rewrite: Anthropic's Thariq, who works on Claude Code, responded from the other side of the breakup: 'Long-time admirer of the Cursor team, few have done more to bring AI coding to the world. Excited to continue to partner with them.'
With over 1,500 likes, it's a pointed contrast: while OpenAI is pulling out, Anthropic is doubling down on the Cursor relationship.
The chess move is hard to miss: in a market where developers are suddenly shopping for alternatives, Anthropic positioning itself as the loyal, low-drama partner is itself a distribution strategy.
original: Long-time admirer of the Cursor team, few have done more to bring AI coding to the world. Excited to continue to partner with them.

rewrite: Anthropic 负责 Claude Code 的 Thariq 在分手事件的另一侧发声：「我一直很敬佩 Cursor 团队，很少有人为把 AI 编程带给世界做了更多。很期待继续与他们合作。」
1500 多个赞，对比意味强烈：OpenAI 撤了，Anthropic 却在加码与 Cursor 的关系。
这步棋不难看懂：在开发者突然开始四处找替代品的市场里，Anthropic 把自己定位成「忠诚、不折腾」的合作伙伴，这本身就是一种分发策略。
original: 我一直很敬佩 Cursor 团队，很少有人为把 AI 编程带给世界做了更多。很期待继续与他们合作。

sections.title: Data Is the Moat / 数据才是护城河
sections.desc: Eon 两位创始人在 No Priors 谈 AI 时代的数据基础设施：模型和算力都变成商品，真正的护城河是数据——以及随之而来的全新安全威胁。

rewrite: The most striking anecdote: Google bought the data of Spirit Airlines out of bankruptcy for a reported $10 million—not the airplanes, just the data, to train models. Another AI company, Mercor, reportedly bid against them.

The Eon co-founders' core argument: models and compute have become near-commodities with 'almost zero switching costs,' so the only durable advantage a company has left is the data it has accumulated over decades.

They describe a messy reality for enterprises: most valuable data is scattered, unclassified, and locked behind business-unit owners afraid to share it. Eon's answer is a 'data foundation' that maps, classifies, and exposes it to AI workflows without compromising security.

The second half of the conversation is a warning: ransomware-style threats now come from non-human actors—AI agents with legitimate permissions dropping tables at extreme velocity. 'We need to assume breach, whether it's malicious or not.'
original: Google bought... the data. They bought the data for $10,000,000 because they think it's very important... They're using it to train models.
Models, compute, everything is relatively ephemeral, almost zero switching costs... the most valuable thing that you have is actually your data.
What we're seeing now on steroids is that the same type of threat is coming from nonhuman actors, agents that essentially have legitimate access... the velocity of that happening is extreme.

rewrite: 最抓人的一个细节：Google 从破产的 Spirit Airlines 手里买下了它的数据，据报道花了 1000 万美元——不是买飞机，只买数据，用来训练模型。据传另一家 AI 公司 Mercor 也参与了竞标。
Eon 两位创始人的核心论点：模型和算力已经接近商品化，「切换成本几乎为零」，所以一家公司剩下的唯一持久优势，就是它几十年积累下来的数据。
他们描绘了企业端的真实乱象：最有价值的数据往往是分散的、未分类的，锁在各个业务负责人手里，大家都怕泄露。Eon 的解法是做一个「数据底座」——把数据映射、分类、暴露给 AI 工作流，同时不牺牲安全。
对话的后半段是警告：过去来自勒索软件的人类威胁，现在以「非人类行为者」的形式成倍放大——拥有合法权限的 AI agent 以极快速度删表。「我们必须假设已经被攻破，无论是不是恶意的。」
original: Google 买的是数据。他们花 1000 万美元买了这些数据，因为他们觉得这很重要……用来训练模型。
模型、算力，一切都是相对短暂的，切换成本几乎为零……你最有价值的东西其实是你的数据。
现在成倍放大的，是同样的威胁来自非人类行为者——拥有合法权限的 agent……发生的速度极快。

sections.title: The Half-Life of Beliefs / 信念的半衰期
sections.desc: 两位资深 builder 不约而同地给出同一个判断：AI 行业的 playbook 和共识都在以「月」为单位过期。

rewrite: Madhu Guru, a senior AI director at Meta who previously led Gemini, Veo, and Nano Banana at Google, argues that AI product building now has roughly a three-month 'playbook half-life.'

His framing: traditional product teams are built to find a playbook and milk it for five years, but AI labs consciously throw playbooks away every few months because they start seeing diminishing returns.

The practical advice for builders: define meta-principles for continuously learning what the market wants today and in three months, and for executing with extreme urgency. Build a team optimized for inventing, not milking.
original: AI product building has a ~3-month playbook half-life.
Legacy teams are optimized for playbook milking. AI teams need to be optimized for inventing.

rewrite: Meta 的 AI 高级总监 Madhu Guru（之前在 Google 领导过 Gemini、Veo、Nano Banana）提出：AI 产品构建现在大约有「三个月」的 playbook 半衰期。
他的框架是：传统产品团队的天性，是找到一个 playbook 然后吃五年；而 AI 实验室会每隔几个月就有意识地扔掉 playbook，因为开始看到边际收益递减。
给 builder 的实操建议：定义一套元原则——持续学习「市场今天要什么、三个月后可能要什么」，并以极致的紧迫感执行。组建一支为「发明」而不是为「吃老本」而优化的团队。
original: AI 产品构建大约有三个月 playbook 半衰期。
传统团队为吃 playbook 老本而优化。AI 团队需要为发明而优化。

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie makes the same point from a different angle: the average strongly held belief in AI now has a half-life of six months 'at best.'

He lists the beliefs the industry has cycled through without reaching consensus: 'OSS is too far behind,' 'the labs can't be profitable at scale,' 'all software will be replaced by agents,' 'you can't build moats on top of models,' 'RAG is dead,' 'we've hit a training wall,' and more.
His conclusion pairs neatly with Guru's: stay flexible in your thinking, because 'we're going to be in a constant state of change for a while.'
original: The average strongly held belief these days in AI has a half life of 6 months at best.
The key here is to remain flexible in your thinking because we're going to be in a constant state of change for a while.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 从另一个角度表达了同样的观点：如今 AI 圈里被强烈持有的信念，半衰期「最多」六个月。
他列了一串行业反复横跳却始终没共识的说法：「开源追不上」「大实验室没法规模化盈利」「所有软件都会被 agent 取代」「模型之上建不出护城河」「RAG 已死」「我们撞上了训练墙」……还有更多。
他的结论和 Guru 的观点严丝合缝：保持思维灵活，因为「我们会在一段时间里持续处于变化之中」。
original: 如今 AI 圈被强烈持有的信念，半衰期最多六个月。
关键在于保持思维灵活，因为我们会在一段时间里持续处于变化之中。

sections.title: The Web Splits in Two / Web 正在两极分化
sections.desc: Vercel CEO 判断 web 会分裂成两个极端，agent 将成为新的浏览器。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch sees the web evolving toward two extremes: ultra-fancy human experiences built for delight and brand (enabled by tools like three.js and typegpu), and agent-centric content, data, and APIs—'pure, lossless signal for machines.'
In the middle, he argues, utilitarian content and data will be 'subsumed by agents producing just-in-time UI'—generated on the fly for you when you need it. 'Think of the agent as the new browser.'
He also flags that MCP is growing explosively, and not just at Vercel—pointing to the mcp-handler npm package as evidence of the broader shift toward machine-readable interfaces.
original: I see the web evolving in two extremes... agent-centric content, data and APIs... pure, lossless signal for machines. The rise of markdown and MCP are the tip of this iceberg.
The 'in between' is likely to be subsumed by agents producing just-in-time UI... Think of the agent as the new browser in this model.

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 判断 web 正在向两个极端演化：一端是为人服务的超精致体验，为愉悦、探索、品牌而生（由 three.js、typegpu 这类工具驱动）；另一端是 agent 导向的内容、数据和 API——「给机器用的纯粹、无损的信号」。
他主张，中间地带——那些工具性的内容和数据——会被「即时生成 UI 的 agent」吞掉：你需要的时候当场给你生成。「把 agent 想象成这个模型里的新浏览器。」
他还提到 MCP 正在爆发式增长，而且不只是在 Vercel——mcp-handler 这个 npm 包的下载量就是机器可读接口大趋势的证据。
original: 我认为 web 正在向两个极端演化……agent 导向的内容、数据和 API……给机器用的纯粹、无损的信号。markdown 和 MCP 的崛起只是冰山一角。
中间地带很可能被即时生成 UI 的 agent 吞掉……把 agent 想象成这个模型里的新浏览器。

sections.title: What to Build / 该做什么
sections.desc: 两条短而锋利的创始建议：别把 AI 挂在嘴上，也别把产品想窄了。

rewrite: VC Nikunj Kothari, a former early engineer at Facebook and CTO of Dropbox, gives founders two blunt rules: the best pitches don't even need to use the word 'AI,' and AI cannot be the only 'why now' in a pitch.
The reasoning, unstated but clear: 'AI' has become table stakes. If your entire story is 'AI,' you haven't explained the actual problem, the customer, or the durable edge.
It lands as a sharp corrective to the flood of AI-first pitches—a reminder that distribution, data, and a real customer pain still decide whether a company works.
original: 1) The best pitches don't even need to use the word 'AI'. 2) AI cannot be the only 'why now' for your pitch.

rewrite: 投资人 Nikunj Kothari（Facebook 早期工程师、前 Dropbox CTO）给了创始人两条直白的规则：最好的 pitch 甚至不需要出现「AI」这个词；AI 不能是你 pitch 里唯一的「为什么是现在」。
背后的道理没明说但很清楚：「AI」已经成了入场券。如果你的整个故事就是「AI」，那你就没有真正讲清楚问题、客户和持久的优势。
这是对铺天盖地的「AI-first」pitch 的一记清醒纠正——提醒你分发、数据、真实的客户痛点，才是决定一家公司能否成立的东西。
original: 1) 最好的 pitch 甚至不需要用到 AI 这个词。2) AI 不能是你 pitch 里唯一的 why now。

rewrite: Peter Yang, who publishes practical AI tutorials, drops a hot take: Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Work are 'partial solutions,' and Grok Bot is the right end state for a capable AI agent product aimed at non-technical people.

His reasoning: people can easily 'grok' that Grok Bot is a computer running in the cloud. Ask the average person to explain the difference between ChatGPT Work and Codex, or how Claude Cowork actually works, and 'most people have no idea.'
The broader point: the winning consumer AI agent will be the one whose mental model is instantly legible—'a computer in the cloud'—not the one with the most features.
original: My hot take is that Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Work are partial solutions and that Grok Bot is the right end state for a capable AI agent product for non-technical people.
If you asked people to explain what the difference between ChatGPT Work and Codex is... I bet most people have no idea.

rewrite: 做实用 AI 教程的 Peter Yang 抛出一个 hot take：Claude Cowork 和 ChatGPT Work 都是「半成品方案」，而面向非技术用户的成熟 AI agent 产品，Grok Bot 才是正确的最终形态。
他的理由：人们很容易「秒懂」Grok Bot 就是一台跑在云端的电脑。但如果你让普通人解释 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 有什么区别、或者 Claude Cowork 到底怎么运作，「大多数人一脸懵」。
更宽的结论：最终胜出的消费级 AI agent，会是那个「心智模型一眼就懂」的产品——「云端的一台电脑」——而不是功能最多的那个。
original: 我的 hot take：Claude Cowork 和 ChatGPT Work 都是半成品方案，Grok Bot 才是面向非技术用户的成熟 AI agent 产品的正确终态。
如果你问别人 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 有什么区别……我打赌大多数人完全不知道。
